## Assessment

| Component | Marks |
|---|:---:|
| Assignments — best two of HW 1, HW 2, and HW 3 | 20 |
| Mini coding project | 10 |
| Mid-semester examination | 30 |
| Paper implementation | 40 |
| **Total** | **100** |

For the assignment component, convert each homework score to a percentage, select the best two, and average them before scaling to 20 marks. This accounts for the different maximum marks of HW 1–3. There are three homeworks and one separate mini coding project. Details and deadlines for the coding project and paper implementation will be announced.

See [Assignments](./assignments.qmd) for handouts and submission dates. The paper implementation is the 40-mark component; there is no separate 40-mark end-semester written examination in this assessment scheme.

## Weekly Plan

Lectures run **Monday, Tuesday and Friday, 1:00–1:50 pm** in 11AC4004. With the
holidays below and the mid-semester week, the semester provides **41 lecture
slots** against the syllabus's 40 hours — one spare. Readings refer to the
[primary text](./resources.qmd) (*The Principles of Diffusion Models*,
arXiv:2510.21890).

The week-by-week plan lives on the **[Curriculum](./curriculum.qmd)** page, which
gives each week's dates, module, theme, and the lecture notes covering it. It is
the single timetable for the course; this page carries the assessment scheme and
the module accounting only. The plan is tentative in pacing, not in coverage.

::: {.callout-note}
Module hours per the syllabus: M1–M4 are 6 hours each; M5–M6 are 8 hours each (40 total). The 40 available slots cover this exactly, so any lecture lost to unforeseen events will be made up on a compensatory day.
:::
